title: The beach clean-up
text:
Characters:
HANA, who loves collecting shells
DANI, her younger brother
PAK MADE, a fisherman

(A beach in Bali, early on a Sunday morning. Small waves roll onto the sand. HANA and DANI walk along the beach, carrying a bucket.)

HANA: (stopping suddenly) Oh no. Look at all this rubbish!
DANI: (kicking a plastic bottle) It's everywhere. Bottles, straws, old flip-flops...
HANA: How will the turtles lay their eggs with all this here?
DANI: (shrugging) It isn't our rubbish. Somebody else should clean it up.

(PAK MADE walks over from his boat, carrying a fishing net.)

PAK MADE: Good morning, you two. Why the serious faces?
HANA: We came to look for shells, but we've only found plastic.
PAK MADE: (sighing) The waves bring more every week. Last month, I found a young turtle tangled up in an old net.
DANI: (quietly) Was it all right?
PAK MADE: It was lucky. I cut it free, and it swam away.

(DANI looks down at the bottle by his foot. Slowly, he picks it up and drops it into the bucket.)

DANI: Maybe it doesn't matter whose rubbish it is.
HANA: (smiling) That's exactly what I was going to say!
PAK MADE: If you two start collecting, I'll fetch some sacks from my boat. My friends can help as well.
HANA: Let's have a beach clean-up every Sunday!
DANI: (grabbing a stick and writing in the sand) I'll write the sign. My letters are the biggest!

(They all laugh. The sun rises higher as they start to fill the bucket.)
